I am interested in the interplay between analysis and geometry, especially partial differential equations and minimal surfaces. My projects and reading also touch on geometric optimisation, probability, and complex geometry.

## Projects and research directions

### Iso-Riemannian Newton's Method

::: {.work-meta}
Melanie Weber and Willem Diepeveen · Ongoing project; manuscript in preparation
:::

I am developing a second-order method in iso-Riemannian geometry, building on [Diepeveen and Weber's first-order optimisation framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.21033). My work studies local quadratic convergence under explicit regularity assumptions, an arclength interpretation in one dimension, and comparisons with Riemannian Newton on pullback geometries. I combine analysis and numerical experiments to understand favourable geometric regimes and counterexamples.

### Minimal surfaces

::: {.work-meta}
Imperial summer research with Marco Guaraco · Exposition in progress
:::

During summer 2026, I studied minimal-surface theory with Marco Guaraco. I am developing a self-contained exposition focusing on stability, Simons's inequality, and the rigidity of stable minimal hypercones in low dimensions.

### Allen–Cahn and minimal surfaces

::: {.work-meta}
MSci project with Marco Guaraco · Proposed direction
:::

My MSci project aims to develop a shorter proof of smoothness for stable Allen–Cahn limit interfaces in ambient dimension three. The precise scope is being refined.

### Riemann surfaces

::: {.work-meta}
Summer 2025 reading project with Masaharu Tanabe · Institute of Science Tokyo
:::

During a summer research placement, I studied Riemann surfaces and their connections with complex analysis and algebraic curves, including holomorphic maps, integration, and the Riemann–Hurwitz formula.

## Expository writing

These pieces were written for courses and reading projects. They explain existing mathematics; the joint report is credited below.

### The Sphere Packing Problem

::: {.work-meta}
Expository paper · MIT 18.156, Harmonic Analysis · Larry Guth
:::

An account of the linear-programming approach to sphere packing, the Cohn–Elkies bound, and the main ideas behind Viazovska's magic function in dimension eight.

[Read the PDF](files/sphere-packing.pdf){.download-link}

### Brownian Potential Theory

::: {.work-meta}
Expository paper · MIT 18.676, Stochastic Calculus · Nike Sun
:::

An introduction to Brownian hitting probabilities, Green functions, and Martin capacity, with an application to boundary regularity for the Dirichlet problem.

[Read the PDF](files/brownian-potential-theory.pdf){.download-link}

### Group Actions and Homogeneous Spaces

::: {.work-meta}
Joint second-year report · Imperial College London · Marie-Amélie Lawn
:::

A report introducing manifolds, Lie groups, and Lie algebras before exploring homogeneous and symmetric spaces. Written jointly with Yiming Fu, Taoxiu Hu, Tarun Nair, and Runshi Qian.

[Read the PDF](files/group-actions-homogeneous-spaces.pdf){.download-link}

### Semidirect Products and Groups of Order 30

::: {.work-meta}
First-year expository poster · Imperial College London · Alessio Corti
:::

A poster introducing internal and external semidirect products and applying Sylow's theorems to classify groups of order 30.

[Read the PDF](files/semidirect-products-groups-order-30.pdf){.download-link}
